name: MO-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+21 district partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Incumbent Mark Alford has a massive fundraising advantage ($1.4M raised vs $42K)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only ~6%
No polls or expert ratings indicate a competitive race
model.rationale: The R+21 district lean, Alford's incumbency, and his roughly 33-to-1 fundraising edge over Jordan Herrera all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and markets agree at about 6% for Democrats. With no polls or ratings suggesting competition, the forecast stays near the fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise wave-level Democratic environment or major outside spending against Alford could narrow the margin, though a seat this red is unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark Alford, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win a second full term in this western Missouri district, which leans Republican by about 21 points. His challenger, Democrat Jordan Herrera, has raised only about $42,000, while Alford has raised nearly $1.4 million and holds a large cash advantage. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but is not a significant factor.

Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 6% chance, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, Alford's incumbency advantage, and the lopsided financial picture, all of which point to a safe Republican seat.
